title: Analogue vs Digital Meters Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav checks the same resistor with two meters. The needle meter says 4 V, the digital meter says 4.97 V. Same resistor, same moment: which one is telling the truth? This animated lesson opens up both kinds of multimeter and solves the puzzle.

We see how one rotary switch turns an analogue multimeter into an ammeter, voltmeter or ohmmeter (shunts, multipliers, a rectifier and a cell around one moving coil meter) and what ohms per volt sensitivity means (a 50 microampere movement gives 20,000 ohms per volt). Then the digital multimeter, block by block: input stage, converters, analogue to digital converter, counter and decoder, display. On a live breadboard both meters measure the same 100 kilo-ohm resistor while the oscilloscope shows the voltage drop when the meter loads the circuit, and we work out both readings (4.0 V and 4.975 V). Then a side-by-side comparison, what a 3 1/2 digit display means, the exam trap (the loading effect), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 20 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 3: Measuring Instruments (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
